# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 1 (Bu-Vb Sk1)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Sk1  
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)  
**Collection:** Vinaya  
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 1  
**Title (English, from literature):** Not wearing the sarong evenly all around  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul2.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul2.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Parimaṇḍala-sikkhāpada* (Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 1) is the opening training rule in the *sekhiya* (rules on etiquette and deportment) section of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka's Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga. The rule enjoins that a monastic should wear their inner robe or sarong evenly all around (*parimaṇḍalaṃ nivāsessāmīti sikkhā karaṇīyā*). An English translation has been prepared by Bhikkhu Brahmali. In the verse summaries (*uddāna*) of the *Parivāra*, the rule is indexed and referenced alongside Sekhiya 2 [Horner 1966].

 It corresponds directly to the first rule of the Pali Bhikkhupātimokkha, the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (Bi-Vb Sk1), and the *Parivāra*, as well as monastic codes preserved in Sanskrit, Tibetan, and Chinese from the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, Lokottaravāda, and Kāśyapīya traditions.
